newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing Yanhua sees steady 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Yanhua sees steady 1997 profit.

text.p: China's Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd expects post-tax profits to be in line with forecasts and said recent falls in its stock price did not reflect performance.
Yanhua had seen a sharp increase in profits and sales since June, the China Daily on Monday a company official as saying. He gave no figures.
The company expected to keep its promise of 684 million yuan ($82.4 million) in after-tax profits this year, it quoted Yanhua general manager and board director Liu Haiyan as saying.

Concerns over the volatile profitability of China's petrochemical industry hurt the performance of Yanhua's stock when it floated 1.012 billion new H shares on the Hong Kong stock exchange in late June, analysts have said.

The stock of the resins and plastic producer fell below the issue price on its first day of trading on June 23 and and had continued to tumble before recovering in the past two weeks, the newspaper said.
"This is a lesson for us," said Yanhua spokesman Xu Dexin. "We recognise the importance of informing investors and providing them with clear and accurate information."
However, Liu voiced confidence, saying: "The gains of this flotation will gradually be made clear as time goes by."
Yanhua's 450,000-tonne ethylene plant was working at full capacity and was expected to produce 500,000 tonnes of ethylene this year and 660,000 tonnes annually by 2000, he said.
The company was set to begin construction of a production line capable of turning out 200,000 tonnes of polypropylene annually, raising total output to 355,000 tonnes, he added.
Yanhua is China's biggest producer of ethylene, synthetic rubber and plastics.
Yanhua was trading at around HK$1.68 on Monday compared with a high for the year of HK$1.93 and a low of HK$1.34.
